impacts.explanation: mintlify:docs-mintlify/artifacts-and-provenance.mdx#retention (owner docs) declares the fact via a concord:fact marker and renders it as null. retention.artifact.days changed from 30 to 90 in T3_CONFIG at packages/contracts/src/product-config.ts#retention.artifact_days; rewriting this occurrence is an editorial decision (anchors/URLs break inbound links; the unit's owner is docs), so it is routed to a human.

diff.before:
---
title: "Artifacts & provenance"
description: "Every analysis output is durable, downloadable, and fully traceable to its origin."
owner: "docs"
---

Every completed turn persists its outputs: plots as PNG, tables as CSV,
scalars as JSON, plus an operation record capturing the exact
`{operation_id, params}` that ran. An artifact cannot exist without complete
provenance — the invariant is enforced in the storage schema itself.

## What provenance answers

Which source file (id and content hash), which operation, which parameters,
which package versions were installed at the moment of computation, when it
ran, and how long it took. Versions are captured from the kernel response
that produced the numbers — never looked up after the fact.

## Lineage

When a turn runs on a previous result table, the new artifacts record the
parent artifact id. The artifact page shows the chain.

## Retention

{/* concord:fact key=retention.artifact.days */}
Artifacts are retained for 30 days after creation; the expiry date is shown
on the artifact page.

diff.unified:
--- a/docs-mintlify/artifacts-and-provenance.mdx
+++ b/docs-mintlify/artifacts-and-provenance.mdx
@@ -27,1 +27,1 @@
-Artifacts are retained for 30 days after creation; the expiry date is shown
+Artifacts are retained for 90 days after creation; the expiry date is shown

patches.changed_because: The authoritative config value retention.artifact_days changed from 30 to 90, so the retention period stated in this unit was updated to 90 days. No other wording, heading, or anchor was altered.
patches.needs_human_because: A human must decide (a) whether the 90-day retention applies retroactively to artifacts already created under the 30-day policy — the evidence states only the configured value, not migration behavior — and (b) whether the existing #retention anchor and any inbound links or cross-references elsewhere that cite '30 days' need coordinated updates.
